title: Lesson 8: The Grace and Mercy Cycle
description: Four words explain what God did for you at the cross: Mercy, Justified, Righteous, and Grace. Through Jesus' story of a forgiven servant and a diagram you build step by step, you will see how these four realities work together in a cycle that starts with God's love and flows through you to others.

blocks.text: In the last lesson, you learned how to study the Bible for yourself. Now you turn from how to read God's Word to what God has actually done for you at the cross, and Jesus begins with a story about a debt.

blocks.alt: A king showing mercy to a kneeling servant whose impossible debt has been forgiven

blocks.title: The Unmerciful Servant
blocks.text:
Jesus once told a story about a servant who owed his king more than he could ever pay back. One day the king ordered the debt to be repaid in full. Since the servant could not pay, the king ordered that the servant, his family, and everything he owned be sold to begin paying the debt. The man fell on his knees and begged for mercy.

But the king did more than give him more time. Out of pity, he released him and forgave the whole debt. Not a payment plan. Not a reduced amount. The entire impossible debt was gone.

Then that same servant walked out and found another servant who owed him a much smaller amount. He grabbed him, demanded payment, ignored the same plea for patience, and had him thrown into prison. When the king heard, he called the servant back and asked, "Should not you have had mercy on your fellow servant, as I had mercy on you?" (Matthew 18:33). In anger, the king handed him over to the jailers until he could pay all his debt. Then Jesus ended the story with a warning: "So also my heavenly Father will do to every one of you, if you do not forgive your brother from your heart" (Matthew 18:35).

The servant heard the words of release, but mercy never reached his heart. It stopped with him. Jesus' ending is sobering, and we should not soften it: forgiving others does not earn God's forgiveness, but a heart that stubbornly refuses to forgive shows it has never truly received His. Canceled debt is meant to turn debtors into merciful people.
8.1 - In Jesus' parable, what stands out to you most about the king's mercy and the servant's response?
The Grace and Mercy Cycle
Paul explains what is underneath Jesus' story.

For by grace you have been saved through faith. And this is not your own doing; it is the gift of God, not a result of works, so that no one may boast. For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand, that we should walk in them.

Salvation is a gift. You did not earn it, and you could never pay it back. It comes by grace through faith. And God did not save you so you could sit still. He saved you so that His grace would flow through you into the lives of the people around you.

The diagram below uses four words to show what God did for you: Mercy, Justified, Righteous, and Grace. These are connected truths about God's gift, not steps you perform to earn it. Tap Begin and follow the cycle slowly, noticing how what Jesus gives you is meant to move through you.
8.2 - Which part of the cycle helps you most to understand God's mercy toward you?
Walking Through the Cycle

Mercy. In Jesus' story, the king does not give the servant what his debt deserves. God looked at your sin and had every right to condemn you. Instead, He had compassion. Mercy means God spares you the judgment you deserve.

Justified. The servant's debt was not small, and your sin is not small either. A holy God does not pretend evil does not matter. At the cross, Jesus bore the judgment your sin deserves. When you trust Him, God forgives you and declares you righteous because of Christ. Justified means God declares you righteous because of Jesus, received by faith. Your acceptance rests on what Jesus has done, even while He keeps changing how you live.

Righteous. The gospel goes further than a canceled debt. God gives you the perfect life of Jesus as your standing before Him. This is the Great Exchange from Lesson 2: Jesus took your sin and gave you His righteousness. Justified and Righteous belong together. One is God's verdict, and the other is the standing you now have in Christ. Being righteous in Christ does not mean your behavior is already sinless. It means Christ is your right standing.
For our sake he made him to be sin who knew no sin, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God.

Grace. The servant walked out free because the king gave him a gift he could never deserve. In Christ, God gives even more: salvation, adoption, new life, and good works prepared for you to walk in. Grace means you receive a gift you do not deserve.

The cycle. This is where Jesus' parable presses hardest. The forgiven servant should have become a forgiving servant. The mercy he received should have shaped the mercy he gave. This is how the cycle works. Consider the diagram: when the arrow reaches Grace, it does not stop. It points back toward Mercy. Those who have received mercy become people who show mercy. Those who have been given grace become people who give grace.
Be kind to one another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, as God in Christ forgave you.
The Mercy That Moves Through You

Jesus' story is a warning, and it is also training in how grace moves. The king's question still lands: Should not you have had mercy, as I had mercy on you? Forgiveness does not mean the wrong was small. It means the mercy you received from God is now larger in your heart than the debt someone else owes you. At the cross, Jesus absorbed the true cost of sin so mercy could reach you without pretending justice did not matter. Now that same mercy starts moving outward. You are God's workmanship, made to do good works, forgive as you have been forgiven, and live as someone whose impossible debt has been canceled.
Showing mercy does not mean calling harm good or immediately restoring trust. You can seek wise help and safe boundaries while you learn to forgive.
8.3 - What is one way you can show someone the mercy you have received from God this week?
Lesson 8 Review

Four words name what God did for you at the cross: Mercy, Justified, Righteous, and Grace. He spared you the judgment you earned, declared you righteous because of Jesus, gave you Christ's perfect life as your standing, and handed you a gift you could never deserve. Then the cycle keeps going, just as Jesus warned in the story of the unmerciful servant. The mercy and grace you have received are the very mercy and grace you now extend to others.
In the next lesson, you will see what it looks like when grace this big starts growing fruit through your daily life.
